page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.r6.4xlarge is a memory-optimized virtual server instance powered by the KVM hypervisor on an x86_64 architecture. The instance is provisioned with 16 dedicated vCPUs running on an Intel Xeon 8269CY processor at a nominal base frequency of 2.5 GHz. With a total memory footprint of 128.0 GB of RAM, the system maintains a 1:8 vCPU-to-memory allocation ratio, delivering 8.0 GB of RAM per virtual core.

The instance provides a baseline network throughput of 5 Gbps and includes zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses. Local storage is not bundled with this configuration, requiring attached cloud storage volumes for operating system disks and persistent file storage. The absence of hardware GPU accelerators keeps processing centered on host compute resources. In terms of resource efficiency, the high memory-to-vCPU distribution avoids CPU over-provisioning for memory-bound tasks.

Because of its high memory capacity relative to compute cores, ecs.r6.4xlarge is structured for memory-heavy enterprise deployments. Typical target workloads include in-memory caching solutions, relational and non-relational database management systems, big data processing engines, and real-time analytical services that depend on storing substantial working sets directly in system memory.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.r6.4xlarge is a memory-optimized virtual machine built on KVM virtualization and the x86_64 hardware architecture. It features 16 dedicated vCPUs based on an Intel Xeon 8269CY processor operating at 2.5 GHz, paired with 128.0 GB of system memory to maintain an 8.0 GB per vCPU distribution. The instance does not include integrated local storage disks, necessitating remote cloud block storage for file systems and data persistence. Network traffic is supported by a 5 Gbps baseline bandwidth allocation, while hardware graphics acceleration is not provided. By balancing substantial memory capacity against a moderate core count, this instance profile offers cost efficiency for memory-constrained workloads without requiring excessive processor scaling. It is well suited for running enterprise databases, large-scale in-memory data grids, caching platforms, and real-time data processing pipelines.
